title: AI Gives 19% Less Diverse Answers than Web Searches
paragraphs: More and more people are using AI chatbots instead of search engines to find information. However, a new study warns that AI may be giving people a narrower view of the world.

The study was led by researchers at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, including Dustin Wright and Professor Isabelle Augenstein. It has been accepted for EMNLP 2026, a major international conference on language technology.

The researchers tested 27 AI language models made by companies including OpenAI, Meta, Google and Alibaba. They asked questions about 155 topics from 12 countries, using 200 different ways of asking about each topic, based on questions from real users. The topics included subjects such as marriage, racism, nuclear weapons and K-pop. In total, the researchers analyzed about 1.7 million AI answers, containing around 70 million separate claims. They then compared the variety of information in these answers with the results of a standard Google search.

The results showed that every AI model provided less varied information than Google. Even the most diverse model, OpenAI's GPT-5, gave at least 18.7% less varied information. Interestingly, smaller models gave more varied answers than larger ones, and newer models were more varied than older ones.
Why does this happen? According to the researchers, AI models learn the most common patterns in the text they are trained on, so less common information tends to be filtered out.

The researchers also warned of a possible "knowledge collapse." In the future, AI models may be trained more and more on text written by AI, which is already less varied. Over time, this could make the range of knowledge even narrower. Augenstein said this has not happened yet, but the mechanism that could cause it already exists.
The researchers advise people to check several different sources of information.
